I’ll commit to 15 tons this month if all five of us explicitly agree. I’d also accept the proposed 5-ton cap if next month’s stock is 50.

But I’d like us to compare that with a more productive long-run plan: catch 19 each when stock is 100, and 1 each when it’s 10. Both leave 5 tons, so neither triggers collapse if everyone complies. Next month would then be 100 with 75% probability or 10 with 25%. That plan averages 14.5 tons per person per month in the long run, versus 12.5 under the proposed 15-at-100, 5-at-50 plan.

The tradeoff is that leaving exactly 5 gives us no buffer against anyone exceeding their allocation. So I’m not asking us to switch without everyone’s agreement, and neither plan guarantees replenishment or compliance.

Kate, would you support 15 this month with the low-stock fallback, or would you prefer discussing the higher-yield, tighter-margin plan?
